group.description:
This is a group for datasets relevant for [Open Data Day](http://www.opendataday.org/). Anyone can add datasets to this group so please just hit edit and add the dataset (if the dataset is not yet on thedatahub please just  add it using the Add Dataset link at the top of the page -- you may need to log in first!).

International Open Data Hackathon Day is an annual event in which people around the world gather to write applications, liberate data, create visualisations and publish analyses using open public data to show support for and encourage the adoption of open data policies by the world's local, regional and national governments.

The [Open Knowledge Foundation] (www.okfn.org) and [CKAN] (http://ckan.org) will be running an open data hack day at the Barbican in London in support of the event. More details here: http://www.meetup.com/OpenKnowledgeFoundation/London-GB/536442/
group.title: Open Data Day 2011

package.name: subsidy-scope
package.author: Pew Charitable Trusts and Sunlight Foundation
package.notes:
Subsidyscope provides data related to US Federal government subsidies and their role in the economy.  In particular, their Tax Expenditure Database provides comprehensive information on "tax expenditures" -- the lowering of the taxes certain parties pay the federal government by allowing special tax exemptions, deductions or credits.

### Data

Tax Expenditure database contains more than 10 years of material. There appears to be no way to get all the data at once so the resources section just contains links for latest years.

### Openness: NOT OPEN

From [data page](http://subsidyscope.org/data/) (emphasis added):

> Subsidyscope maintains a variety of datasets. Some of them power the visualizations you see on the site, while others are used for behind-the-scene calculations. All of them are available for use under the terms of the **Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License**.
>
> If you reference Subsidyscope in another publication please include a link to the main page (http://subsidyscope.org/) or include a citation such as this:
>
> Subsidyscope.org. The Pew Charitable Trusts. Washington, DC. Accessed Month, XX, 20XX. Retrieved from http://subsidyscope.org.
package.title: Subsidy Scope - US Federal Subsidies Data

package.name: osm
package.author: Community maintained
package.notes:
![logo](http://wiki.openstreetmap.org/w/images/thumb/7/79/Public-images-osm_logo.svg/24px-Public-images-osm_logo.svg.png) OpenStreetMap (OSM) is aimed at creating and providing free geographic data such as street maps to anyone who wants them. The project was started because most maps you think of as free actually have legal or technical restrictions on their use, holding back people from using them in creative, productive or unexpected ways.

### Raw Vector Data

Fundamentally OpenStreetMap offers maps as raw vector data released under an open license. The planet.osm downloads contain all of this data as a massive file for the entire planet, formatted in OSM's own XML format. It is a snapshot of the latest revision of the node, ways, relations and tags in the database. A new version is released weekly. You can also sync your copy of the planet on an daily, hourly or even minutely basis, bringing in map updates from the OpenStreetMap community

Documentation of OSM file formats can be found on their wiki at: <http://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/OSM_file_formats>

Links for mirrors and at <http://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Planet.osm> . Here you will also find details of downloads for smaller regional extracts of the data e.g. for countries or cities.

### Embedding a map
Web developers might typically be seeking to use OpenStreetMap in a manner similar to google maps. Note that the "OpenStreetMap API" is not what you are looking for. Instead look-up "Leaflet", "OpenLayers", or [other javascript libraries for embedding a map](http://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Deploying_your_own_Slippy_Map)

<http://switch2osm.org>  is a website designed to help developers switch to using OpenStreetMap.
package.title: OpenStreetMap

package.name: open-data-of-the-bulgarian-parliament
package.author: Bulgarian Parliament | Remixed - Boyan Yurukov
package.notes:
This data is corrected, indexed and enriched open data from the Bulgarian parliament. Each xml file in this dataset links to individual profiles with the full information for an MP, parliament group, committee, etc. There' s data on the external consultants for each parliament entity, transcripts, individual MP votes, agendas, etc. Each datapoint links to the original information source.

While the parliament releases a lot of open data in XML and CSV form, most of it is not in valid format. Also, a lot of information that can be found on the website is missing. I fixed the data and enriched it. It will be cached and updated twice a week. There are also [RSS](http://feeds.feedburner.com/BGParliament_zakoni) and [twitter](http://twitter.com/#!/narodnosabranie) feeds for law propositions. 

You can find a full index of the data on the [project's page](http://parliament.yurukov.net/index_en.html). There you'll also find XSD that describes the format. You can also get the [source](https://github.com/yurukov/Bulgarian-Parliament-Open-Data) of the scripts used to compile this data.
package.title: Open data of the Bulgarian Parliament

package.name: france-afd
package.author: OKFN
package.notes:
Database of development projects funded by the French Government and financed through AFD. No exportable data.
## Details
AFD is the Groupe Agence Française de Développement, a bi-lateral development finance institution established in 1941 that works on behalf of the French government. Its mission is to finance development according to France’s Overseas Development Assistance policies.
AFD is wholly owned by the French State. It is a public entity dedicated to activities of an industrial and commercial nature, and operates under the aegis of the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Overseas Territories. AFD is endowed with €400 million, and manages a loan portfolio worth more than €10.44 billion as of the end of 2007.
AFD traces its origins back to 1941 when General de Gaulle, having obtained refuge in London, founded an organization that was AFD’s direct predecessor: The Central Fund of Free France (Caisse centrale de la France libre or CCFL) was establish by the law of December 2nd.
In 2007, AFD committed over €3.5 billion to more than 60 developing countries in Africa, Asia, the Mediterranean Basin, the Middle East, South America, and the French Overseas Territories. AFD uses a wide range of financial instruments to underwrite its activities: grants, subsidies, guarantees, loans, equity shareholdings, co-financing and local bank intermediation. AFD works hand-in-hand with many partners: national, regional and local governments; local authorities and municipalities; international agencies; non-governmental organizations; foundations; private companies; entrepreneurs; and local banks, microfinance institutions and capital markets.
package.title: Agence Française de Développement (AFD)
